triage_digest.tier_profile: 12 T1 / 6 T2 / 5 T3 / 0 T4 — unusually strong evidence base for a tech-press topic
signal: Adoption-trust inversion is the single most differentiated finding: 84% adoption [C1, T1, 3 convergent large-n surveys] vs 29% trust [C2, T1, 4 sources]. This is a paradox, not a statistic.

The perception-vs-measurement gap has RCT-grade backing [C4, T1]: METR -19%, DORA +21% non-significant, DX 10% wall. Three independent studies pointing at 'no measurable speedup for experienced devs'.
Senior skepticism is reframed as a *competence signal* [C3+T2 commentary], not luddism — this is the emotional core for the target audience.
Quality decay evidence is strong and concrete [C5, T1]: 45% OWASP, 8x duplication (GitClear).
noise_and_thin_ice: N1 [source-chain defect]: C4's three RCTs all resolve to ONE secondary URL (blakecrosley.com blog). The numbers match known primary findings, but Writer must cite METR/DORA/DX primaries, not the blog. Flagged for editor-qa retrace.

N2 [vendor bias]: Ox Security '68-73% security flaws' and IEEE '62% lack rate limiting' route through dev.to/pcables secondary links. Vendor-published, n=300 repos. Downgrade to directional claim or drop the 68-73% figure; keep Veracode 45% which is cleanly sourced.
N3 [sample size]: METR RCT n=16. Must be presented with n disclosed ('small but randomized') — not as settled fact.

N4 [tier ceiling]: C6 (tool market) and C7 (MCP/ACP) rest on Tier-2/3 sources incl. community blogs and pricing comparisons. Temporal risk is real: product positioning ages in weeks. Use as background texture, never as load-bearing claims.
N5 [audience mismatch]: Gap-1 — no data isolates staff+/principal engineers; 'senior' stats aggregate from ~5yrs. Avoid claiming 'principals feel X'.
N6 [recency]: AllAboutAI multi-survey via globenewswire is a promo-style aggregator; superseded by SO+JetBrains primaries. Do not cite.
triage_digest.dedup_note: 84%/29%/19% figures converge across surveys — strongest evidence in corpus; safe to lead with.
triage_digest.followup_rationale: Gaps are framing constraints, not evidence holes. Article is sellable without clarification round; the 5 gaps are encoded as avoid_claims + one live-tracking box instead.

chosen_angle.working_h1: Your AI Skepticism Is Calibrated: What 49,000 Developers and 3 RCTs Say About the Senior Engineer's Real Job
chosen_angle.alt_h1: The Trust Gap Is the Quality Gate: Why Senior Engineers Distrust AI Code — and Why the Data Says They're Right
chosen_angle.thesis: The collapse in senior-developer trust (2.6% highly trust) is not lagging adoption to be caught up with; it is the most accurate signal in the industry. RCTs confirm seniors' gut: measured productivity for experienced devs is flat-to-negative, and the senior's durable role is being re-priced from code author to verification architect and environment designer.
chosen_angle.audience: Senior/staff software engineers (5-15 yrs) who already use AI tools daily and feel quiet cognitive dissonance about it; secondarily engineering leaders deciding rollout policy.
chosen_angle.rationale: Highest composite on search intent (this audience is actively searching to resolve their dissonance), novelty (inverts the dominant 'seniors are resistant' frame), and evidence backing (every load-bearing section sits on Tier-1). Also converts the corpus's best asset — convergent paradox data — into narrative tension instead of a stats list.

blueprint.tone: peer-to-peer authority: dry, precise, evidence-first, zero hype and zero doom. Speak as a senior engineer to senior engineers — allow one wry line per section, no exclamation marks, no 'revolutionary'.
blueprint.argument_progression: hook paradox -> own the emotional frame (calibrated skepticism) -> hard evidence (RCTs) -> cost evidence (quality decay) -> counterpoint (perception data + tool-side rebuttal) -> synthesis (role shift) -> practical protocol -> forward-looking box

data_slots.slot: AI output quality bounded by architecture quality x context clarity

avoid_claims: Do NOT cite '68-73% of AI code contains security flaws' (Ox Security) — vendor study, secondary sourcing, conflicts in magnitude with Veracode 45%.
Do NOT cite the IEEE '62% lack rate limiting' figure — URL chain is pcables.com, unverifiable to primary.
Do NOT cite any AllAboutAI / globenewswire aggregate (91% growth, 97.5% company integration) — promo aggregator.
Do NOT state METR 19% without disclosing n=16 and 'small randomized study'.
Do NOT claim staff/principal engineers distrust more — data only segments 'senior' (~5+ yrs).
Do NOT rank tools (Cursor vs Copilot vs Windsurf) as fact — Tier-3 sources, fast temporal decay; use categories only.
Do NOT present MCP/ACP 'protocol war' as settled — Tier-2/3, 2 sentences max if used.
Do NOT imply AI makes juniors faster as measured fact — no RCT in dossier supports junior-specific speedup.
Do NOT reuse the dossier's blakecrosley.com URLs in final citations — retrace to METR/DORA/DX primaries.
writer_contract.style: peer-to-peer, dry, evidence-first; one wry line per section max; no hype/doom; every stat gets an inline source mention; 2,400 words ±10%; [H]/[X] labels must survive into published text as explicit hedging.
writer_contract.qa_watch: editor-qa: retrace N1 (RCT primaries) and N2 (Veracode chain) against originals per Charter Art. II — these are the two highest overstatement risks in the draft.
